name: Logo Marquee
hint: Move toward the strip and it slows, then stops. Grab it and flick it. Hover a mark for their numbers.
description: A trusted-by logo strip with physics instead of a CSS loop. One drive with a velocity moves the row: it eases down as the pointer approaches and stops under it, can be grabbed and flicked with inertia by mouse, touch or a sideways trackpad swipe, then coasts back to cruising speed. Page scroll pushes it faster and scrolling up briefly reverses it. Hovering, focusing or tapping a mark dims the others and drops a glass card with that customer's proof line and industry; arrow keys walk the marks and glide each to the centre. Edges dissolve through a mask, a pause button is always visible, and the loop stops off screen. Layouts: one row, two geared rows running opposite ways, or a ruled grid whose cells swap one at a time. Reduced motion gets the still grid. Shows only the brands you pass (a mark node, an image src, or the name as text); with no brands it renders nothing. The fourteen invented sample brands, drawn in SVG in one ink, appear only with `demo`.
intents: trusted by logo strip for a landing page
infinite scrolling logo marquee with edge fade
customer logo wall with hover details
draggable logo carousel that pauses on hover
social proof band under a hero
usage: Place directly under a hero or above pricing as a quiet supporting band, full width of its container. Pass `brands` as { id, name, mark | logo | src, industry, proof, since }: `mark` (or `logo`) is your SVG in currentColor so every logo takes the same ink, `src` is an image URL, and with neither the name is set as text. `industry`, `proof` and `since` fill the card that drops from a hovered or focused mark; leave them out and there is no card. Pass `heading` (one line; its first number rolls in once). `onSelect(brand, event)` reports a click or Enter on a mark. Pause is `paused` + `onPausedChange` or `defaultPaused`. Use the `double` layout when you have more than ten logos, `grid` when the page already has a lot of motion. Pass `scroller` if the page scrolls inside an element rather than the window. The strip slows and stops under the pointer, holds while a mark has focus, and reduced motion gets the still grid. `demo` shows the invented sample brands and heading (gallery only).

dataProps.type: { id: string, name: string, mark?: ReactNode, logo?: ReactNode, src?: string, industry?: string, proof?: string, since?: string | number }[]
dataProps.description: The logos, in order. `mark` or `logo` is a node (SVG in currentColor), `src` an image URL; with neither the name is shown as text. `industry`, `proof` and `since` fill the hover / focus card; without them a mark has no card.
One-line heading above the strip; its first number rolls in once. Blank shows no heading.
Heading level of the heading element.
Controlled pause. Pass it with onPausedChange; leave it out to let the strip keep its own.
Uncontrolled starting pause (a later change is followed too).
Called when the Pause / Play button is pressed, with the new value.
Called when a mark is clicked, tapped or activated with Enter / Space, with that brand object.
The scrolling element, when the page scrolls inside one instead of the window (scroll pushes the strip).

dataProps.type: { play, pause, playStrip, pauseStrip, list, row(k), more(n), andMore, since(year) }
dataProps.description: Words the strip uses (button text and names, the list name, the grid's '+N more' cell, the card's 'Since' line). Merged over the English defaults.
Marks are not focusable, open no card and cannot be dragged; the Pause button is disabled.
Fill blank `brands` and `heading` with the invented sample brands. Gallery only; leave off in real UI.

How the marks are arranged: "marquee" is one moving row, "double" is two geared rows running opposite ways, and "grid" is a still, ruled wall whose cells swap one at a time. Reduced motion always gets the grid.

example:
<LogoMarquee
  heading="Trusted by 1,200 teams"
  brands={customers.map((c) => ({ id: c.id, name: c.name, src: c.logoUrl, industry: c.sector, proof: c.quoteLine }))}
  onSelect={(brand) => openCaseStudy(brand.id)}
/>
